sections.heading: Section – A : OBSERVATION AND REPORTING ( 15 marks )

blocks.instruction: Fill in the gaps with the correct answer. ( 6 x 1 = 6 )
blocks.notes: Each item prints two bracketed choices, e.g. '( Kerala / Karnataka )' — effectively a 2-option choose-and-fill; keep choices in q. (c) choice wraps over two lines ('( Energy Giving / Body-Building )'). (a) textbook: Ugadi Pachadi is from Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telengana → Karnataka.
Answer brackets '(   )' after each statement. (e) is a negative-framed statement (answer False).

blocks.instruction: Write a short note on the following. ( 2 x 2 = 4 )
blocks.notes: (a) 'Importance of water in our diet.' (b) 'Balanced food' (no full stop). 4 ruled answer lines each. Judgement items, need rubric.

sections.heading: Section – B : IDENTIFICATION AND CLASSIFICATION ( 12 marks )

blocks.notes: TYPO (a) 'What did Surabhi’s grandmother use to eat to during summers and winters?' — stray 'to' and 'use' for 'used'; textbook spells the name 'Surbhi' (deev105 p.74: jowar and bajra roti in winters, jau roti in summers). Keep as printed + teacherNote. (e) 'Who is a ‘Chef’?' — curly quotes. (b)–(d) open-ended.

Two-column table, headers 'Protective Foods' | 'Energy Giving Foods', one empty row. Marks '2 x 1' read as one point per column (describe each food type). Ambiguous: could also mean two differences. Owner to confirm.

blocks.instruction: Give an example of the ingredients or food items that match each of the tastes listed below? ( 6 x ½ = 3 )
blocks.notes: Instruction ends with '?' though it is an imperative — keep. Table header cells: Sweet | Sour | Salty | Pungent | Bitter | Astringent, one empty answer row. Map to 6 one-word items with broad acceptable lists.

blocks.instruction: Draw any two junk food and also write the names. ( 2 x 1 = 2 )
blocks.notes: 'two junk food' (grammar) kept. Two empty boxes each with a drawn name line '_________' (drawn-line blank, appears in cache as underscores). App cannot grade drawing: nearest type draw/one-word (name) + rubric; say so in instruction.

sections.heading: Section – C :  DISCOVERY OF FACTS ( 13 marks )

blocks.notes: Each item has two answer blanks (½ each implied, not printed). (b) 'Water – rich fruits' with spaced en-dash (kept). (d) 'super food' refers to textbook millet stall (jowar upma etc.). Open lists → broad acceptable.

Left: a. Boiling b. Steaming c. Frying d. Roasting e. Grilling f. Baking. Right (with '(   )' answer brackets): cakes, rice, popcorn, idiyappam, puri, chicken. Expected: Boiling–rice, Steaming–idiyappam, Frying–puri, Roasting–popcorn, Grilling–chicken, Baking–cakes. Mark bracket '( 6 x ½ = 3)' has no space before ')'.

blocks.instruction: Circle the odd one out. ( 4 x ½ = 2 )
blocks.notes: Printed '10.Circle' (no space after number) and Q10/Q11 are indented as if sub-items — keep labels 10, 11. Items list words with ' , ' spacing and italic '( Clue: … )'. Likely answers: a lemon, b tomato, c cheese, d pizza. (a) potato is arguably fine; (b) almonds are also body-building per some books — accept as printed key.

blocks.instruction: Locate the following states in the given map. ( 3 x 1 = 3 )

pictures.what: Outline political map of India with state boundaries, no names (low-resolution raster, framed box)

blocks.notes: Sub-line printed in bold: 'a. Andhra Pradesh , b. Karnataka , c. Telangana' (states where Ugadi Pachadi is traditional, Ch 5). MUST draw an India state-outline SVG with numbered/marked regions so the child can pick which region is each state; answerable from drawing alone. Map is an image — not in text cache.
